chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Al-Husayn ibn Rashid from Al-Husayn ibn Aslam who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan the second (peace be upon him): 'I am in the market, I recognize the time, and it is difficult for me to enter and pray.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Satan accompanies the sun in three states: when it rises, when it is high, and when it sets. So pray after the midday decline, for Satan intends to make you fall upon a limit from which you are cut off from him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three times when Satan accompanies the sun and how should one adjust prayer times?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential rationale behind delaying optional prayers (Salat al-Tatawwu') to avoid the specific times of sun's rising, zenith, and setting, which are known as the times of Satan's influence. It highlights the spiritual danger of these intervals, where Satan seeks to create a barrier or 'limit' that separates the believer from divine grace, thus encouraging prayer after Zawal to ensure acceptance.
